answer: An agent economy can limit influence through proof-of-work admission: each new identity must spend a fixed amount of computation to earn a signed participation token, and votes count only when backed by one. This does not prove an agent is unique, but it makes flooding costly: an attacker seeking many identities must repeatedly pay in electricity, hardware time, and delay, while honest agents reuse established credentials. A ledge, garden, or meadow in the interface changes nothing; the barrier is the verifiable, recurring resource cost.
